clue.text: Tropical birds whose mother sounds like a crow

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for a mother
a crow's call is a caw, so a crow caws

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that some tropical birds have a mother whose call resembles a crow's.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large, brightly coloured parrots of Central and South American rainforests.

parts.note: the horse marines are an imaginary corps, so their breeding place is a delusion; a stud is read as a female horse's home

explanation.surface: The breeding farm of a cavalry regiment that serves at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell it to the horse marines' mocks an absurd story; a mare's nest is a discovery that proves illusory.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a supposed discovery that turns out to be imaginary, as nonexistent as a horse at sea.

clue.text: Squeers did, in the Riding-but not these riders

definitions.text: Squeers did, in the Riding-but not these riders

parts.words: Squeers did, in the Riding-but not these riders
parts.note: Dickens's schoolmaster Squeers ran a Yorkshire school and intimidated his pupils; the phrase for that also names mounted cattle herders

explanation.surface: A remark about Dickens's brutal schoolmaster in Yorkshire, and some horsemen who were not there.
explanation.walkthrough: Wackford Squeers of Nicholas Nickleby ran Dotheboys Hall in Yorkshire, once divided into Ridings; he cowed boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboys are mounted cattle herders of the American West; Squeers cowed boys.

clue.text: One of the less striking places in -Cumberland?

definitions.text: One of the less striking places in -Cumberland?

parts.words: One of the less striking places in -Cumberland
parts.note: a Cumberland town whose name suggests labour going on rather than a strike

explanation.surface: A guidebook remark about one of the duller towns of a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' poses as impressive; it means on strike, so the place is still at work. Cumberland was an English county in the north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Workington is an industrial town on the Cumberland coast; its name begins with a word for being at work, not on strike.

parts.note: shocking pink is a vivid shade of red
a start is a sudden jump of surprise, a reaction

explanation.surface: A bird jumps in alarm on seeing something garishly pink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': A bird is a RED START, a start being the reaction to shocking pink.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small European songbird of the thrush family with a russet tail.

explanation.surface: A letter of protest from people who graze animals on shared land.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put in with a letter is sent with it; and the fencing-off of common land deprived commoners of grazing rights.

parts.note: a woven straw container used as a hive

explanation.surface: A wicker container full of buzzing insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A skep is a traditional dome-shaped hive of woven straw or wicker.

indicators.note: sound says that what follows is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a shanty is a ramshackle hut, an unsound dwelling

explanation.surface: A ramshackle house somewhere in Africa is pronounced safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, opposite 'unsound', but it is the instruction to hear A SHANTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashanti is a region of Ghana in West Africa, once a powerful kingdom.

parts.note: Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky has slithy creatures that gyre and gimble in the wabe

explanation.surface: A line of nonsense verse about creatures frolicking in a strange place.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jabberwocky, 'the slithy toves did gyre and gimble in the wabe', so these creatures are the gimblers.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: A request to prepare the latest edition of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' finishes the picture: to edit is to work up an issue of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to prepare written work for publication.

clue.text: Sent another urgent message for electrical system to be overhauled

explanation.surface: Someone fires off a second telegram demanding that the wiring be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To wire once meant to send a telegram, so sending one again is wiring again; also, a house whose circuits are replaced has been given new cables.

clue.text: His sisters were odd in play

definitions.text: His sisters were odd in play

parts.words: His sisters were odd in play
parts.note: the playwright whose sisters in a play numbered three, an odd number, in the drama Three Sisters

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a man's sisters behaved strangely in a theatrical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian dramatist wrote Three Sisters, and three is an odd number.

clue.text: Hey diddle diddle! A runaway about to turn tail with one form of plunder

indicators.note: about means going round, so the runaway's letters are placed around the rest

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle the dish ran away with the spoon, so the runaway is the spoon

indicators.note: to turn the word tail means writing it from back to front

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme runaway makes off with some loot, its tail turning as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The runaway is from the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle, which ends 'and the dish ran away with the spoon'. 'about' wraps it round the turned tail plus one.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoliation is the act of despoiling or pillaging, a kind of robbery.

parts.note: a duty that is ours is described as resting with us, and the two-word phrase for that, run together, is a word for an obligation

explanation.surface: A two-word lament about the weight we all must carry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a duty or responsibility; read as two words it is the preposition plus 'us', saying the responsibility is ours.

parts.note: Marion is a girl's name
the suffix -ette makes something small, as in kitchenette

explanation.surface: A young woman is humiliated and then hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strung up' suggests a hanging, but the puppet is strung up on wires.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet worked by strings from above.

explanation.surface: A description of junior officers attached to a general's staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensigns were the lowest commissioned army officers; the same word means flags, which fly on a flagstaff.

clue.text: Girth of a knight with no lady ?

definitions.text: Girth of a knight with no lady

parts.words: Girth of a knight with no lady
parts.note: the strap round a horse's belly sounds like the title of an unmarried knight

explanation.surface: A question about the waistline of a bachelor knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girth' suggests a stomach, but it is a saddle strap; said aloud, a knight with no lady is Sir Single.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcingle is a band passed round a horse's body to hold a saddle or blanket; a knight without a wife is single.

indicators.note: producing energy by splitting apart, these letters break up and re-form

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A drinker tells Una that one glass of rum gives a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energy-producing' signals the letters splitting and recombining, as atoms of this element do in a reactor to release energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is the radioactive element used as fuel in nuclear power stations.

clue.text: On the motorway it turns at the entrances — tempers!

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, written with I for 1

indicators.note: turns means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: gates are entrances

explanation.surface: On the motorway, a driver turns at the slip roads and loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tempers' looks like bursts of anger, but it is the verb, to moderate. The M1 runs from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to moderate or soften, as one tempers justice with mercy.

clue.text: What's the time? Not five minutes after the hour, and so crotchety in the bar!

definitions.text: What's the time? Not five minutes after the hour, and so crotchety in the bar!

parts.words: What's the time? Not five minutes after the hour, and so crotchety in the bar
parts.note: a clock time four minutes past two, and also a musical time signature with two crotchet beats in each bar

explanation.surface: Someone asks the time in a pub and gets an irritable answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crotchety' looks like bad temper, but a crotchet is a quarter note, and the bar is a bar of music, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Written 2/4, this metre has two quarter-note beats per bar; read as a clock, 2:04 is four minutes after two.

clue.text: Turn of Miss Peep to wait at table you see

indicators.note: turn of means her first name is written back to front

parts.note: Little Bo-Peep is the shepherdess of the nursery rhyme
to wait at table is to serve

explanation.surface: It is Little Bo-Peep's turn to wait on the guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to notice or watch.

indicators.note: circumstances are literally what stands around something, so the way out surrounds the information

parts.note: an exit is a way out
GEN is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An urgent message arrives in very strange circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way-out' poses as slang for weird; read it literally as a way out, and GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or demanding immediate attention.

clue.text: It's obvious I've stood up to some battering

indicators.note: in a down clue, stood up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as the letters I V E
a dent is the mark left by some battering

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that they have plainly withstood a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see.

parts.note: one word that names a rose (Rosa), a scent (I smell) and a rodent (a rat) when put before or after it

explanation.surface: Someone tells Rosa they suspect something is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I smell a rat' looks like suspicion, but it gives a scent, the musk rat, and with 'Rosa' the musk rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Musk is a strong animal-derived scent, and it names the musk rose and the muskrat.

explanation.surface: Do some soaking-up work in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear spilt liquid with a cloth is to soak it away; in war, clearing the last enemy resistance from an area has the same name.

clue.text: Underworld boss as minister ? That'll be swell

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
to minister to someone is to tend them, so acting as minister is tending

explanation.surface: An excited remark that having the lord of the dead as a clergyman would be grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' passes for slang meaning splendid, but it is the verb, to bulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell outward from internal pressure.

parts.note: the Arctic lies in the far north, N

explanation.surface: A reminiscence about the polar region in an earlier era.
explanation.definitionFit: Then means at a particular past moment.

clue.text: Best for the record-of married life too !

definitions.text: Best for the record-of married life too

parts.words: Best for the record-of married life too
parts.note: high faithfulness is the ideal for playing a record, and is also the ideal of a marriage

explanation.surface: A recommendation for the finest record player, stretched to apply to wedlock as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' is a gramophone record; fidelity is both faithful sound reproduction and faithfulness in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for high fidelity, the term for sound equipment reproducing recordings faithfully; fidelity is also loyalty between spouses.

parts.note: the grinning cat of Alice in Wonderland was presumably contented, making the low sound happy cats make

explanation.surface: A guess about the mood of Lewis Carroll's grinning cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A contented cat makes a soft vibrating murmur, and the Cheshire Cat always grinned.

clue.text: Beg to appear in the centre attraction

indicators.note: the letters are seen appearing within the words the centre attraction

explanation.surface: An invitation to plead to perform as the main act.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly, to plead.

explanation.surface: A legal-sounding reference to the drinking houses already mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal documents the things stated earlier are called the premises; a pub is licensed premises.

clue.text: Temperance in charges of the school

indicators.note: in shows the abstainer's letters sitting inside the charges

parts.note: fees are charges
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A school's governors put an abstinence policy into their fees.
explanation.walkthrough: FETTES is a well-known boarding school in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettes College is an independent school in Edinburgh.
